original_question: Does every bounded C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space have a bounded rational calculus?
target_in_paper: Section 7 (Further problems), Problem 28(i) "Rational calculus and contractivity".
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact object class and ambient setting of the paper's formulation almost verbatim: bounded C0-semigroups, Hilbert space, and the question of bounded rational calculus. It is clearly targeting Problem 28(i), not a neighboring problem.
missing_details: The calculus is really attached to the generator (or to the operator A with -A generating the semigroup), not to the semigroup family as an abstract object.
In the paper's comment, "bounded" is specifically interpreted as boundedness with respect to the H∞-norm.
The relevant function domain is the right-half-plane functional calculus: functions lying in or compared against H∞(C_+), where C_+ is the open right half-plane.
A stand-alone formulation should fix the sign convention explicitly, e.g. whether A or -A is the generator of the bounded C0-semigroup.
The paper notes a hidden caveat about the precise rational-function domain and about what to do when the generator is not injective.
For a self-contained functional-calculus question, the scalar field should be taken to be complex.
The paper immediately comments that the answer in this generality is negative, so the question should not be presented as still open without qualification.
refined_question: Let H be a complex Hilbert space, and let -A generate a bounded C0-semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on H. After fixing the standard rational functional calculus for A on the open right half-plane C_+ (including the non-injective case if needed), must this rational calculus be bounded with respect to the H∞(C_+) norm; equivalently, does there exist a constant C such that ||r(A)|| ≤ C ||r||_{H∞(C_+)} for every bounded rational function r on C_+ for which r(A) is defined?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for -A the generator of a bounded C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space, must A admit a bounded H∞(C_+)-calculus?
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Problem 28(i) in Section 7. Your draft is already very close to the paper's wording, but it is not fully stand-alone because the paper's comments supply the crucial hidden conventions: the intended norm is the H∞-norm; the ambient holomorphic domain is the open right half-plane C_+; the calculus is for the generator (with sign convention to be fixed); and there are technical issues about the rational-function domain and non-injectivity. The paper also explicitly states that, in this generality, the answer to Problem 28(i) is no, and that bounded rational calculus is equivalent here to bounded H∞-calculus. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the half-plane generator-calculus question above, not the broader similarity-to-contractions question in Problem 28(ii).
